chunks: Ahmad narrated from Al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) for days, and he used to perform Qunut in every prayer, both in those wherein recitation is loud and in those wherein it is not loud.

key_terms.وَلَا يَجْهَرُ فِيهَا: And in which he does not make it loud
key_terms.يَجْهَرُ فِيهَا: In which he makes it loud (referring to recitation)

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams perform Qunut in all prayers including those with quiet recitation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the consistent practice of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in performing Qunut during all obligatory prayers, irrespective of the recitation volume. This establishes a strong precedent for the permissibility and recommended nature of Qunut in daily Salah within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view of it being a Sunnah Mu'akkadah only in Fajr. The report underscores the Imam's adherence to a comprehensive ritual practice that integrates supplication into the core structure of obligatory worship.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Al Husayn, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal who said,
‘I prayed Salāt behind Abu Abdullahasws for days, and heasws used to perform Qunut in every Salāt, the ones in which is loud recitation, and in those wherein is no loud recitation’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad has narrated from al-Husayn from ibn abu Najran from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following: “

Whenever I performed Salah (prayer) led by abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, I found him (the Imam) say Qunut (supplication after recitation in second Rak‘at) in every Salah (prayer); those which are said aloud as well as those said silently.”
